Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States Mixed Fed on hold / labour cracks
🇪🇺 European Union Bullish ECB on hold / rotation winner
🇨🇳 China Bearish less stimulus / weak credit
🇯🇵 Japan Bullish reflation / BOJ hike bias
🇵🇱 Poland Bullish MPC pause / March optionality
🔬 US–Asia Semis — SOXX / ASML / TSMC Bullish
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Paid for AI revenue, punished for AI cost
🔍 Underowned Themes — Attention and Exposure Gaps
Japanese banks under a hiking BOJ
Critical minerals and mined copper supply
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
$AMZN — capex shock before AWS payback Bearish
$MSTR — leveraged Bitcoin proxy under forced-seller stress Bearish
$ETR — Feb. 12 print tests the regulated AI-load story Bullish
Silver / SLV — the meme metal after the crash
Bitcoin ETF / IBIT — new money under water

Software dip / FIG — ‘dumb money’ steps in
body: Friday, February 06 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information cutoff: 2026-02-06 00:00 UTC. Market figures use completed observations before this date.

Macro Stance: The US is running at two speeds: surveys accelerated while the labour market cracked. The January ISM manufacturing PMI printed 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02], the kind of reading that normally supports cyclicals and upward earnings revisions. Against that, ADP counted just 22,000 private jobs in January Bloomberg.com [Feb 04], and with the official payrolls report rescheduled to Feb. 11 after the shutdown Bloomberg.com [Feb 04], the market is trading weak private labour data against firm surveys. We are Mixed, with the risk skewed toward a soft labour print that revives rate-cut expectations.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.47% and the 10Y at 4.21%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 74 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y was unchanged (0 bps) while the 10Y rose 6 bps, widening the spread by 6 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05). The curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, and the 20-observation move is a steepening (10Y up, 2Y down/flat); over five observations the 2Y fell 6 bps against 3 bps for the 10Y as the front end priced the weaker jobs data (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05). Investors are ramping up bets on a steeper curve under a Warsh-led Fed Reuters [Feb 04]. The S&P 500 closed at 6,798.40, down 1.77% over 20 sessions, while the VIX rose 3.13 points to 21.77 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

New / Most Important: The AI trade has turned on its own beneficiaries: a selloff wiped nearly $1 trillion from software and services stocks as investors debate AI's existential threat to their business models Reuters [Feb 04]. The S&P 500 fell 1.23% in the prior session and 2.45% over five sessions, the Nasdaq 100 lost 5.16% over five sessions, and the Dow was little changed over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). This is a rotation inside equities rather than a liquidation: value, energy and staples are absorbing the money that leaves software.

Playbook ✓: Own the rotation, not the index: overweight industrials, staples and energy, and keep long-duration software underweight until the selloff stops making new lows. Hold 2s10s steepeners into the delayed payrolls report Bloomberg.com [Feb 04]; a print near the ADP pace extends the front-end rally, while a strong report that pushes the 2Y back above its level of five observations ago is the signal to take profits. Keep S&P 500 put spreads while the VIX sits above 20; a VIX back at its 20-session-ago 15.38 would flip the call to adding beta (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Macro Stance: The ECB kept rates unchanged and signalled comfort with the dollar's weakness Reuters [Feb 05], so it is not leaning against a strong euro. Euro-zone inflation fell to 1.7% in January Financial Times [Feb 04], which lets the bank sit on hold with an easing option rather than a tightening one. Low inflation, stable policy and cheaper valuations than the US make Europe the main beneficiary of the rotation out of US tech: Bullish.

Activity & Inflation: German factory orders unexpectedly rose the most in two years Bloomberg.com [Feb 05], the clearest hard-data sign that the industrial downturn is turning. In the UK, the Bank of England held at 3.75% in a surprisingly close vote Reuters [Feb 05], which tells markets a cut is near and kept sterling on the back foot. GBP/USD fell 1.31% over five sessions to 1.3645 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

New / Most Important: Global ex-US equity funds drew inflows as investors shunned pricey US tech Reuters [Feb 05]. The STOXX 600 is up 1.3% over 20 sessions at 611.65 and the FTSE 100 up 2.63%, against a 1.77% fall for the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The laggard is Germany: the DAX is down 2.53% over 20 sessions despite the orders rebound, a gap we expect to close if the data hold (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Playbook ✓: Overweight European banks, industrials and UK large caps, and underweight European data and software names until the AI-disruption selloff stabilises. A close BoE vote means UK cuts are near, which supports domestic UK cyclicals over sterling. Change the call if EUR/USD, at 1.1802 and up 1.07% over 20 sessions, breaks sharply higher and the ECB starts to talk the euro down (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Macro Stance: China is choosing restraint: Beijing has signalled a trimmed GDP growth target that requires less stimulus Bloomberg.com [Feb 05]. Exports carry the headline numbers, but credit, property and household demand are not turning, and a lower target means policy will not force them. We stay Bearish on the domestic cycle and on Hong Kong-listed platforms, where tax and AI fears now compound.

PMIs & Activity: The official January manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 Reuters [Jan 30], back below the 50 line. The private gauge disagreed: factory activity grew at the fastest pace since October, beating the official reading CNBC [Feb 01]. The gap between the two surveys is what an economy carried by external demand looks like — exporters holding up, domestic orders soft — rather than a broad recovery.

Credit Impulse: The latest credit data are weak: new bank loans in 2025 were the lowest in seven years Reuters [Jan 15], and the feed carries no January lending print yet. Marginal rate relief cannot create an impulse without willing borrowers, and the property slump removes the main collateral channel. A January new-loan figure above last year's pace would be the first confirmation that demand is responding.

Property: Housing is still sliding: Shanghai is piloting state home purchases in three districts to halt the market slide Caixin Global [Feb 05], which makes the city government a buyer of last resort. State buying can put a floor under prices in one city, but it does not restore developer cash flow or land-sale revenue for local governments. What would change the view: stabilising tier-one sales after the Shanghai pilot, followed by other cities copying it.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal room is tight: China logged its first fiscal revenue drop since 2020 on the property slump and weak consumption Reuters [Jan 30], which explains both the restraint on stimulus and the search for new tax revenue. On trade, the US proposed a critical-minerals trade bloc aimed at countering China Reuters [Feb 04], a direct challenge to Beijing's main supply-chain lever. Over time the bloc caps the pricing power of Chinese processors, a slow-moving negative for the export model.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng closed at 26,885.24, up 0.14% in the prior session but down 3.87% over five sessions, and the Shanghai Composite at 4,075.92, down 0.64% on the day and 0.17% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). ASHR closed at 33.20, down 1.57% over 20 sessions, KWEB at 33.37, down 8.05% over five sessions, and USD/CNY at 6.9377, a 0.84% yuan gain over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Hong Kong-listed Chinese tech entered a bear market as tax and AI fears took hold CNBC [Feb 04].

New / Most Important: The new element is fiscal: Tencent and other Chinese tech stocks dropped after a VAT-hike rumour Yicai [Feb 03], so platforms now carry a tax overhang on top of the global AI-disruption discount. That helps explain why KWEB has lost 6.05% over 20 sessions while FXI is down only 2.75% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). A firm yuan plus less stimulus tightens conditions for exporters at the margin, so the cushion for equities is thin.

Playbook ✓: Underweight KWEB and Hong Kong tech until the tax scope is clear; an official statement limiting the VAT changes is the trigger to cover. Prefer long-CNY expressions (short USD/CNY) over Chinese equity beta, and keep developers out of portfolios until the Shanghai purchase pilot shows sales stabilising. ⚠ Divergence: the private PMI at its fastest pace since October CNBC [Feb 01] says activity is firmer than the official PMI and the credit data suggest.

Macro Stance: Japan votes on Sunday with Prime Minister Takaichi endorsed by Trump Reuters [Feb 05], and a BOJ board member has added to signals pointing to rate hikes Bloomberg [Feb 05]. Reflation with a central bank that is tightening rather than easing is a constructive mix for domestic earnings, especially for lenders: Bullish.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 156.917, up 2.5% over five sessions, as hedge funds revived yen-weakness trades ahead of the vote Bloomberg [Feb 03]. The Nikkei 225 ended at 53,818.04, down 0.88% on the day but up 3.57% over 20 sessions, outperforming the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). A weak yen props up exporters' earnings, while BOJ hike signals protect the currency from a disorderly slide.

Playbook ✓: Own Japanese banks and capex beneficiaries with only a partial yen hedge. A decisive Takaichi win is seen as the best scenario for bonds and the yen Reuters [Feb 05], so cut yen-short hedges on that outcome. A weak result that forces spending deals raises JGB supply risk, and the BOJ will not come to the rescue of a Takaichi-driven bond rout Reuters [Feb 04] — in that case trim duration-sensitive insurers.

Macro Stance: The RBA raised the cash rate to 3.85% after three cuts AP News [Feb 02] and forecasts materially higher inflation AFR [Feb 03], which leaves the door open to further hikes. Tightening into households that only just received relief is Bearish for domestic cyclicals and housing-linked equities.

Demand & Financing: Major banks passed the hike straight through to home-loan rates Reuters [Feb 03], so the tightening reaches mortgage holders immediately. AUD/USD closed at 0.6994, up 4.05% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 at 8,889.20, up 2.23% over 20 sessions but down 0.43% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The stronger currency adds a second layer of tightening for exporters and tourism.

Playbook ✓: Underweight Australian rate-sensitive retailers and REITs; prefer the major banks, whose margins benefit from higher cash rates. Hold AUD longs while the RBA keeps a hiking bias, adding on dips toward its 20-session-ago 0.6722 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Change the call if the next monthly CPI shows inflation rolling over, which would reopen the case for a one-and-done hike.

Monetary & Activity: The Monetary Policy Council (RPP) left rates unchanged in February, and StockWatch's read is that the council is waiting for March StockWatch.pl [Feb 04] — a pause, not the end of easing. Activity is strong: GUS data show GDP grew 3.6% in 2025 Rzeczpospolita [Jan 30]. Solid growth with contained inflation lets the NBP cut gradually rather than urgently — the best mix for Polish banks' earnings.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5706 and EUR/PLN at 4.2133, the latter up only 0.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). EPOL fell 2.38% to 37.37 in the prior session but is up 2.1% over 20 sessions, and the WIG20TR ETF closed at 67.11, down 2.5% on the day and up 4.39% over 20 sessions; PKO BP gained 7.57% and Pekao 8.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The WIG set a historic record twice in one day midweek Interia Biznes [Feb 04].

Companies: KGHM is the volatility source: the copper miner lost 15% at the open as the metals selloff hit the Warsaw floor Money.pl [Feb 02], and it closed at 310.20, down 16.59% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Orlen's model refining margin collapsed by 60% in two months Bankier.pl [Feb 05], yet the stock is still up 15.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Allegro is down 10.54% over 20 sessions and CD Projekt 11.83% over five, the local face of the global tech selloff (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Security & New Development: Poland signed a $4.3 billion ‘drone wall’ deal to deter Russia Bloomberg.com [Jan 30], a reminder that defence spending is now a structural fiscal line rather than a one-off. That spending supports domestic industry and engineering firms but adds to borrowing needs, which keeps the złoty sensitive to global risk appetite. The security premium has not hurt the currency so far: EUR/PLN is near flat over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Polish banks (PKO BP, Pekao) through EPOL or the WIG20TR ETF: any March cut would be gradual while growth stays solid. Avoid KGHM until metals volatility fades, and wait on Orlen until refining margins stabilise. Change the call if the złoty weakens sharply on global risk-off. ⚠ Divergence: record WIG highs coexist with a 60% collapse in Orlen's model refining margin Bankier.pl [Feb 05] and a five-session slump in KGHM — index strength is narrow and bank-led.

Narrative: Consensus has flipped from ‘AI lifts all tech’ to ‘AI eats software’: the selloff wiped nearly $1 trillion from software and services stocks Reuters [Feb 04]. XLK fell 7.44% over 20 sessions and QQQ 5.15% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The driver is terminal-value risk for seat-based software, not next quarter's numbers.

Reported: Microsoft shares sat about 10% lower after its earnings call The Motley Fool [Feb 02], and the stock is down 18.57% over 20 sessions as investors question when AI capex pays back (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Oracle fell 6.95% in the prior session and 29.23% over 20 sessions, the market's discount on debt-funded AI build-outs (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

EPS Upside Watch: Hardware with pricing power is the escape route: Apple has become a surprise winner during the tech wipeout MarketWatch [Feb 05], up 5.98% over 20 sessions and 6.83% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Device makers sell the AI endpoint rather than a seat licence AI can replace, so their estimates are not exposed to the same disruption.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Hedge funds have made $24 billion shorting software stocks so far in 2026 and are increasing the bet CNBC [Feb 04]. Crowded shorts against capitulating longs is a classic squeeze setup, so do not add new shorts here; express the bearish view through underweights rather than outright short positions.

Narrative: Communication services is where AI shows up as revenue, but the capex bill splits the group: Alphabet plans to double capex to as much as $185 billion Fortune [Feb 04]. XLC slipped 0.75% over 20 sessions while META rose 3.32% and GOOGL 2.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Reported: Meta soared after proving its AI spend while Microsoft struggled to please CNBC [Jan 29], and Reddit rose on strong guidance and a $1 billion buyback CNBC [Feb 05]. The common thread is ad revenue that AI targeting is already lifting, which the market pays for even alongside heavy spending.

EPS Upside Watch: Ad-funded platforms with AI targeting have better estimate momentum than subscription media. GOOGL is still up over 20 sessions despite the capex shock, a sign investors credit search and cloud monetisation (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Upside revisions are likeliest where ad pricing, not user growth, drives the quarter.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The losers in the group are content owners, not ad platforms: NFLX fell 10.87% and DIS 7.03% over 20 sessions while META rose (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). AI is a revenue engine for targeting and a cost threat for content; pair long ad platforms against subscription media.

Narrative: The financials debate has moved from margins to credit: the software rout is spreading pain to the debt markets WSJ [Feb 05], because private lenders financed many of the software businesses now being repriced. XLF fell 4.17% over 20 sessions, JPM 5.15% and GS 5.38% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Reported: Blue Owl says it sees no tech ‘red flags’ as its shares extend a record plunge Bloomberg.com [Feb 05]. Management reassurance while the equity reprices is a late-cycle tell; the market wants loan-level marks, not commentary.

EPS Upside Watch: Deposit-rich lenders: BAC rose 3.5% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05), and a 74 bps 10Y−2Y spread that widened 6 bps over 20 observations supports net interest income (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05). Banks with little private-credit exposure are the place to look for upside revisions.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A steepening curve should lift bank margins, yet bank stocks fell alongside private credit — GS lost 2.51% and JPM 2.24% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The market is pricing credit losses, not spreads; that is the signal to avoid alternative asset managers until the marks are visible.

Narrative: Energy is the rotation's biggest winner: XLE rose 15.69% over 20 sessions with Brent up 12.66% to 67.55 and WTI up 13.04% to 63.29 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Investors are buying cash-flow value as AI anxiety drains growth stocks, and the Iran standoff adds a supply premium.

Reported: Shell posted its weakest quarterly profit in nearly five years but kept buybacks steady CNBC [Feb 05]: buybacks, not earnings, are what hold the sector's valuation together. XOM is up 23.28% and CVX 15.48% over 20 sessions on the same logic (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

EPS Upside Watch: Gas-levered names: Henry Hub closed at 3.51, down 10.44% over five sessions, so gas equities price little of the structural power demand from data centres (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Upside revisions are likelier for gas producers than for oil-weighted names if winter demand persists.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oil settled almost 3% lower on easing supply concerns ahead of the US-Iran talks Reuters [Feb 05], and the sector rally is running ahead of earnings. A diplomatic breakthrough would strip the premium quickly, so own integrateds with buyback cover (XOM, CVX) rather than high-beta producers.

Narrative: Industrials are the cleaner rotation trade: XLI rose 5.91% over 20 sessions and CAT 13.71% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05), backed by a January ISM manufacturing PMI of 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02]. Data-centre power equipment and a factory rebound give the group two independent drivers.

Reported: GE Vernova's Q4 gas turbine orders surged 74% Utility Dive [Jan 30], the strongest evidence that data-centre power demand is turning into multi-year backlog. That backlog is what the market is paying for in CAT and the grid suppliers.

EPS Upside Watch: Power generation and electrical equipment have the clearest order visibility, and CAT's 20-session gain shows the market already rewards that exposure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Boeing, up 3.87% over 20 sessions, is the aerospace recovery name with the most room for delivery-driven upside (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The ISM jump came from post-holiday reordering Reuters [Feb 02], which can fade as quickly as it arrived, and GE fell 5.34% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Favour data-centre power and automation over short-cycle and transport names until the reorder effect is tested.

Narrative: Discretionary is caught between a squeezed consumer and Amazon's capex shock: Chipotle forecast weak sales as consumers cut discretionary spending Reuters [Feb 03]. XLY fell 2.8% over 20 sessions, AMZN 7.81% and TSLA 7.93% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Reported: Amazon's shares fell on an earnings miss and $200 billion of 2026 capex guidance CNBC [Feb 05], while Tapestry lifted annual forecasts after a Tabby-handbag-driven blowout holiday quarter Reuters [Feb 05]. The split is income, not category: affordable luxury is growing while mass-market spending is cut.

EPS Upside Watch: Upper-income-exposed brands and home improvement: HD rose 9.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05), and lower mortgage rates would release pent-up housing-related spending. Estimates for affordable luxury look too low after Tapestry's quarter.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The K-shape now drives sector returns more than the cycle: NKE is down 0.82% over 20 sessions while HD rallied (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Do not buy the sector; buy the upper-income leg and avoid low-income-exposed chains until spending data improve.

Narrative: Staples have become the funding destination of the AI rotation: XLP rose 13.44% over 20 sessions, WMT 12.62% and COST 12.09% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Walmart hit a $1 trillion market value, joining a club dominated by Big Tech Reuters [Feb 03].

Reported: PepsiCo's drink sales are improving, and it is planning to cut snack prices CNBC [Feb 03]. Volume recovery is being bought with price, which is the right trade-off for share but caps margins.

EPS Upside Watch: Scale grocers with membership and online income are the likeliest staples beats: COST is up 3.82% over five sessions even in a falling tape (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). They are the likeliest staples beats; branded food is not.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples rally on safety while branded producers need price cuts to hold volume, so the sector's multiple is rising as its margin outlook falls. A strong payrolls print that revives cyclicals would hit staples first — hold the overweight in retailers, but do not add to branded food.

Narrative: Health care is split between policy pressure and the GLP-1 leader: the White House debuted TrumpRx with roughly 40 medications WSJ [Feb 05]. XLV fell 3.02% over 20 sessions, UNH 21.41% and LLY 7.87%, including a 7.79% LLY drop in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Reported: Lilly's Mounjaro and Zepbound pushed Q4 revenue up 46% BioSpace [Feb 04], yet the stock is down over 20 sessions. Managed care remains the weakest link, with UNH down 8.12% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

EPS Upside Watch: Volume-driven names with pricing pass-through, such as drug distributors, are better placed than manufacturers facing direct price pressure. Lilly's volume growth still argues for estimate upgrades even if price per script falls.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Lilly fell 7.79% in a single session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05) despite reporting 46% Q4 revenue growth BioSpace [Feb 04] — volume winners are no longer automatically price winners once Washington sells drugs direct. Size GLP-1 exposure for lower pricing and prefer the volume leader over challengers.

Narrative: Materials are up 8.18% over 20 sessions, but metals whipsawed: silver fell 32.89% over five sessions to 76.53, gold 8.06% to 4,889.50 and copper 6.1% to 5.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Reuters commentary ties the crash to a ‘debasement’ trade unwinding on the prospect of a Warsh Fed Reuters [Feb 02].

Reported: Anglo American cut its 2027 copper guidance as production declines WSJ [Feb 05], a supply signal rather than a demand one. Lower mined supply against data-centre and grid demand is supportive for copper prices over a multi-year horizon.

EPS Upside Watch: Copper as the AI-capex metal: FCX is still up 6.7% over 20 sessions despite a 9.07% drop over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05), and supply cuts at peers raise the value of operating mines. Industrial gases and chemicals with pricing power are the steadier compounders.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The hedge has become the volatility source: GLD fell 10.89% over five sessions and NEM 14.5% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Buy gold miners only after volatility settles, and keep precious-metal exposure in physical-backed ETFs rather than levered miners.

Narrative: REITs are cheap but not yet helped by rates: US REITs ended January at a median 16.2% discount to net asset value S&P Global [Feb 05], while the 10Y sits at 4.21%, 6 bps higher over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05). XLRE rose 2.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Reported: Crown Castle dipped after soft EBITDA guidance and announced job cuts Seeking Alpha [Feb 04], a reminder that tower REITs face carrier consolidation and slower leasing. The print reinforces the split between data-centre and logistics landlords with pricing power and legacy telecom infrastructure.

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and industrial REITs have the cleanest rent growth, and a front-end rally would ease their refinancing costs. A 10Y that stops rising would turn the NAV discount into a catalyst rather than a value trap.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A steeper curve hurts REITs more than a lower front end helps them, because most borrow at longer tenors; the 30Y at 4.85% sets the funding bar (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05). The NAV discount may be a refinancing discount rather than a bargain — prefer low-leverage names with light near-term maturities.

Narrative: Regulated utilities are working while merchant power breaks: XLU rose 2.94% and NEE 13.83% over 20 sessions, but CEG fell 27.04% and VST 7.46% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The question is who captures data-centre load without political blowback.

Reported: Xcel's quarterly profit rose on AI-driven power demand Reuters [Feb 05], the regulated model working as designed: load growth becomes rate-base growth. The market is paying for that visibility over merchant price exposure.

EPS Upside Watch: Entergy reports full-year 2025 results on Feb. 12 Entergy [Feb 05], the next test of whether regulated utilities can turn data-centre interest into signed load and higher capex plans. NEE's 20-session gain shows investors already reward that pipeline (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Affordability politics is the risk: Senator Hawley is circulating a data-centre costs bill Axios [Feb 05]. That hits generators selling into data-centre contracts first — the CEG drawdown is the warning — and it could later cap allowed returns for regulated names too.

Narrative: European autos are losing on China competition and EV economics: the STOXX Europe 600 autos ETF fell 2.76% in the prior session to 45.96 and 3.08% over 20 sessions, while BMW is down 3.95% and Renault 5.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Reported: Volvo Cars fell over 22% in its worst trading day ever CNBC [Feb 05]. The read-across is margin pressure for every European maker exposed to China and tariffs, and the sector ETF fell 2.76% in the same session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

EPS Upside Watch: Volkswagen is the relative winner: VOW3 is up 0.29% over 20 sessions against a falling sector (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). That relative resilience marks it as the name best placed to beat lowered estimates.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Stellantis is the worst performer: STLA fell 6.74% in the prior session and 11.5% over 20 sessions, while Mercedes dropped 3.22% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Stay underweight the sector until margins stabilise; VW is the only long.

Narrative: Semis are the payee of the capex wave: Alphabet's plan to double capex Fortune [Feb 04] adds to Amazon's $200 billion guide. SOXX is up 1.83% over 20 sessions despite an 8.39% drop over five, with MU up 12.76% and TSM 3.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Reported: AMD sank 17% after earnings CNBC [Feb 04], and Qualcomm fell 8% as it issued a dire warning on the memory shortage CNBC [Feb 05]. The market is separating AI-infrastructure winners from chipmakers whose end markets are being starved of components.

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and foundry: the shortage that hurts Qualcomm is pricing power for memory makers, and MU's 20-session gain shows it (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). ASML, up 9.91% over 20 sessions, carries the equipment upside from foundry expansion (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The AI build-out is starving handsets of memory, so the same capex cycle is a headwind for smartphone chip designers. NVDA, down 9.11% over 20 sessions, lags memory despite the capex guides (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05) — own memory and foundry, underweight handset chips.

Rewarded: Companies that showed AI turning into revenue now: Meta soared after proving its AI spend CNBC [Jan 29], and Reddit rose on strong guidance and a $1 billion buyback CNBC [Feb 05]. Niche guidance raisers also won — Tapestry lifted annual forecasts after a blowout holiday quarter Reuters [Feb 05].

Punished: Beats did not help where guidance or AI exposure disappointed: AMD sank 17% after earnings CNBC [Feb 04], Microsoft sat about 10% lower after its call The Motley Fool [Feb 02], and Amazon fell on a miss plus $200 billion of capex guidance CNBC [Feb 05]. Lilly's 46% Q4 revenue growth BioSpace [Feb 04] did not prevent a 7.79% one-day drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Pattern: The market pays for AI that shows up in this quarter's revenue and punishes two things: AI capex without visible monetisation (Amazon, Microsoft) and business models AI can replicate (software, information services). Beats are table stakes; guidance and the capex-to-revenue ratio decide the reaction.

Attention into EPS: Entergy's full-year results on Feb. 12 test the utility-AI story Entergy [Feb 05]. Beyond that, attention will sit on any software name that reports in-line guidance — the first one to rally on it would mark the turn in the disruption trade.

Playbook: Buy post-earnings dips only in names that raised guidance and show AI-driven revenue — ad platforms, distributors, data-centre power — and fade beats that arrive with capex step-ups and flat guides. The trigger to broaden risk is a reporting day where software names rise on in-line guidance.

Attention Gap: Election coverage dominates Japan, but the earnings story sits in the banks: Japan's three top banks are on track for record profits for the fiscal year Nikkei Asia [Feb 05]. A BOJ board member adding to rate-hike signals Bloomberg [Feb 05] extends the margin tailwind well beyond the vote.

Exposure & Risk: Instruments: the MUFG, SMFG and Mizuho ADRs, or the Nikkei 225 as a broad proxy at 53,818.04, up 3.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Risk: a fiscal-driven bond rout after the vote would inflict mark-to-market losses on bank bond portfolios — size positions so a sharp JGB selloff is survivable.

Attention Gap: Washington is building a policy floor under strategic metals with a proposed critical-minerals trade bloc to counter China Reuters [Feb 04], while mined copper supply shrinks as Anglo American cuts its 2027 guidance WSJ [Feb 05]. The precious-metals crash pulled attention away from that floor.

Exposure & Risk: Instruments: FCX at 59.22, up 6.7% over 20 sessions but down 9.07% over five, and copper futures at 5.80, nearly flat over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Risk: policy-driven names reverse fast and Chinese retaliation can swing prices, so scale in over weeks rather than chase.

Market Context: Bitcoin closed at 62,702.10 at the prior completed daily close, down 14.13% on the day, 20.25% over five sessions and 34.36% over 20 sessions; Ether closed at 1,821.68, down 15.01% and 44.72% over 20 sessions, and Solana at 78.19, down 15.04% and 46.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The listed proxies fell harder: IBIT dropped 13.16%, COIN 13.34% and MSTR 17.12% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

New / Most Important: Bitcoin dropped 15% and briefly broke below $61,000 as the sell-off intensified and doubts about crypto grew CNBC [Feb 05]. Bessent said the US government cannot tell banks to bail out crypto Yahoo Finance [Feb 05], removing a policy put the market had assumed under a crypto-friendly administration. Strategy's $12.4 billion Q4 loss CoinDesk [Feb 05] shows how the treasury-company model amplifies the drawdown.

Playbook: Do not catch the knife with leverage: treasury companies such as MSTR are the forced-seller risk, so prefer spot exposure via IBIT over equity proxies. Add only after Bitcoin reclaims its five-session-ago level and ETF outflows stop; until then, keep crypto sized as a tail position. COIN, down 40.58% over 20 sessions, prices a lot of volume damage already (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Rates & Dollar: The DXY closed at 97.82, up 1.6% over five sessions but down 0.87% over 20, while TLT rose 1.09% in the prior session to 87.48 and IEF 0.59% to 96.07 as the front end rallied (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The 10Y−2Y spread of 74 bps widened 6 bps over 20 observations, a steepening (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05), and investors are adding to steepener bets under a Warsh-led Fed Reuters [Feb 04].

Credit Check: HYG closed at 80.53, down 0.43% over 20 sessions, while LQD was nearly flat at 110.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05) — high yield lags as the software rout spreads into debt markets WSJ [Feb 05]. The damage is concentrated in software-linked and private credit rather than broad corporate spreads, so this is a sector problem, not yet a funding one.

Portfolio Implication: Money is rotating, not leaving: global ex-US equity funds drew inflows as investors shunned pricey US tech Reuters [Feb 05]. Keep an overweight in Europe, Japan and EM versus US growth, own IG over HY, and stay duration-neutral until the delayed payrolls; widen the HY underweight if HYG breaks lower while the S&P 500 is stable.

What Is Priced: Oil has already priced some de-escalation: crude settled almost 3% lower on easing supply concerns ahead of the talks Reuters [Feb 05], leaving Brent at 67.55, down 2.75% on the day but still up 12.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The two sides agreed to Friday talks in Oman but remain at odds over the agenda Reuters [Feb 04].

Conditional Expression: If the talks yield a framework, the remaining premium unwinds: trim XLE overweights into strength, sell Brent upside and buy fuel-sensitive airlines and European chemicals. If they break down, own Brent call spreads and XLE, add gold on weakness and expect the dollar to firm. After a 20-session energy rally, the downside on a deal is larger than the upside on a failure.

Risk: Military incidents can overtake diplomacy at any point, and a single strike would gap oil higher before positions can be adjusted. Use options rather than futures, and keep gold at 4,889.50 as the cheaper geopolitical hedge after its 8.06% five-session drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

What Is Priced: Markets are positioned for a Takaichi win: Trump endorsed her ahead of Sunday's election Reuters [Feb 05], and hedge funds revived yen-weakness trades ahead of the vote Bloomberg [Feb 03]. USD/JPY closed at 156.917, up 2.5% over five sessions and 0.72% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Conditional Expression: A decisive win is seen as the best scenario for bonds and the yen Reuters [Feb 05] because it removes the need for coalition spending deals — then cover yen shorts and add Japanese banks. A narrow or failed mandate would push spending bargains, weaken the yen and pressure JGBs — then hold USD/JPY longs and underweight life insurers.

Risk: The BOJ will not come to the rescue of a Takaichi-driven bond rout Reuters [Feb 04]. Even a big win could trigger a supply-driven JGB selloff if the spending plan is larger than expected, so keep yen hedges partial.

Catalyst & Thesis: Amazon's Q4 report carried an earnings miss and $200 billion of 2026 capex guidance CNBC [Feb 05]. The market is punishing capex that runs ahead of payback, as it did with Microsoft. Thesis: free cash flow compresses through 2026, and the stock trades as a funding source until AWS growth visibly accelerates.

Price Hurdle & Risk: AMZN closed at 222.69, down 4.42% in the prior session and 7.81% over 20 sessions, below its 20-session-ago 241.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Risk: an AWS reacceleration or a trimmed capex guide would flip the view; cover on a reclaim of the 20-session-ago level.

Catalyst & Thesis: Strategy reported a Q4 loss of $12.4 billion, or $42.93 per share CoinDesk [Feb 05]. With Bitcoin down 34.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05), the equity premium that funded coin purchases is gone. Thesis: new issuance gets harder, and the stock lags the coin until Bitcoin stabilises.

Price Hurdle & Risk: MSTR closed at 106.99, down 17.12% in the prior session and 33.89% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Risk: a sharp Bitcoin rebound would squeeze shorts, so express the view with put spreads, not outright shorts, and step aside if Bitcoin reclaims its 20-session-ago 95,525.12.

Catalyst & Thesis: Entergy reports full-year 2025 results on Feb. 12 Entergy [Feb 05]. Peers have set the bar: Xcel's profit rose on AI-driven power demand Reuters [Feb 05]. Thesis: regulated utilities with data-centre load earn rate-base growth while merchant generators absorb the political backlash.

Price Hurdle & Risk: ETR is not on our market card, so we give no price level; the sector reference is XLU at 43.10, up 2.94% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Risk: affordability politics such as Hawley's data-centre costs bill Axios [Feb 05] could cap allowed returns, and a guide that leans on unsigned large-load contracts would weaken the case.

Observed Attention: CNBC reports retail traders are not giving up on SLV even after silver's plunge CNBC [Feb 02]. The ETF remains the default retail vehicle for the metal, and dip-buying has continued through the drawdown.

Motivation & Bias: Anchoring to January's highs plus a debasement narrative: buyers see the crash as a gift rather than a regime change. The Warsh-driven unwind that triggered the crash Reuters [Feb 02] has not reversed, so the narrative is fighting the catalyst.

Instrument & Risk: SLV closed at 66.69, down 15.77% in the prior session and 36.83% over five sessions, with silver futures at 76.53 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Volatility at this level invites tighter leverage terms; use small, defined-risk positions.

Observed Attention: MarketWatch reports the Bitcoin ETF suffered its worst decline in over a year, leaving new investors sitting on ugly losses MarketWatch [Feb 05]. The losses sit with recent buyers, the cohort most likely to sell into further weakness.

Motivation & Bias: Buy-the-dip conditioning meets loss aversion: new holders anchored to higher entry prices either average down or capitulate. Capitulation usually shows up as heavy ETF outflows into a high-volume low, which is the signal to watch rather than the price alone.

Instrument & Risk: IBIT closed at 36.10, down 13.16% in the prior session and 29.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Further outflows feed the price decline; stage entries only after outflows slow.

Observed Attention: Reddit shares rose on strong guidance and a $1 billion buyback CNBC [Feb 05], one of the few tech prints the market rewarded. The platform's own users overlap with the retail investor base, which keeps attention on the stock high.

Motivation & Bias: Retail owns what it uses, and AI-driven ad tools give that familiarity an earnings story. The bias is familiarity — investors overweight a product they like and underweight competitive risk from AI search.
Instrument & Risk: RDDT is not on our market card, so no price level. The risk is that AI search changes traffic sources; the buyback cushions the downside, so selling puts beats chasing calls.

Observed Attention: Stocktwits says retail traders feel Figma, down over 40% this year, is a steal Stocktwits [Feb 04], while the broader software selloff has wiped nearly $1 trillion of value Reuters [Feb 04].

Motivation & Bias: Mean reversion and anchoring: a stock that halves looks cheap to buyers anchored to its listing price. Institutions are doing the opposite and pressing shorts, which is the definition of a crowded disagreement.

Instrument & Risk: Use baskets rather than single names and stage entries; XLK fell 7.65% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Hedge funds have made $24 billion on software shorts and are increasing the bet CNBC [Feb 04] — a squeeze can help, but without an earnings catalyst the trend is down.
